name: ThemeForge
overview: Automatically finds, scores and assigns theme songs for movies and TV shows.
description: ThemeForge searches YouTube with yt-dlp, ranks every candidate with an explainable scoring engine, and writes the winner to theme.mp3 beside your media. High-confidence matches are assigned automatically; anything less certain waits in a review queue. Every theme is loudness-normalised at encode time so themes play at a consistent volume, which Jellyfin itself provides no way to control. All decisions are recorded in a persistent index, so re-runs are idempotent and manual choices are never overwritten.

versions.changelog: Fixes downloads failing with HTTP 403. The plugin now uses its own yt-dlp rather than an older copy found on PATH, and replaces it automatically when it ages out - previously the update task downloaded a current yt-dlp that was then never used. Adds a "Retry failed items" action to clear the retry backoff, a warning when yt-dlp is too old, and takes a settings snapshot per run so a mid-run change cannot make the report disagree with what happened.

Per-library rules for existing themes: leave them alone, replace only the ones ThemeForge chose, or replace everything. Adds a dedicated log file with its own level, full cleanup on uninstall, an action to remove every theme ThemeForge wrote, and a durable index that survives an interrupted run.

First release. Automatic discovery and scoring, loudness-normalised themes, per-library rules for existing themes, review queue, a persistent decision index, a dedicated log file, and full cleanup on uninstall.
